parsed.explanation: The combined regime stacks a hostile national layer on a hostile state layer. Nationally: passport sex-marker policy with reported confiscations and strandings, a visa cable directing refusals and potential lifetime fraud findings where sex is doubted, an athlete-entry ban, documented custody harms (conversion-style prison policy, forced labour, sexual abuse), and state-terror framing of 'pro-transgender' ideology — organised state hostility, not just disapplication. The state adds a tier-1 universal exposure: a criminal-trespass facilities ban covering state buildings, schools, parks and airports, backed by a licence-fraud treatment of marker mismatches, care restrictions reaching adults, and a hate-crime law excluding gender identity. One documented arrest (dismissed on standing) shows enforcement is sporadic, but universal-exposure rules are rated by reach, not prosecutions. Foreign passports do not shield the visitor from entry screening, state facilities, or custody. Sits between 0.25 and 0.35 anchors.

entry_documents.exposure: National passport marker policy (though visitor carries home documents) and a visa cable instructing refusal where sex is doubted and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility; foreign governments issued travel advisories after detentions of travellers over visa issues.
entry_documents.protection: Fraud finding requires four elements and is never automatic; limited waivers exist; litigation unresolved.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry refusal strands the traveller; a visa dispute can escalate into a fraud/misrepresentation investigation.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections bureau adopted conversion-style policies for trans inmates (hair cuts, hormone removal); immigration-custody trans men reported forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse; reporting of trans prisoner counts stopped.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any visa or facility encounter that produces detention places the visitor in this documented custody regime.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: State statute bars gender-identity-congruent restrooms/changing rooms in all state/local government buildings, schools, parks, airports; refusal to leave is criminal trespass; state also treats licence marker mismatch as fraud; bans in many other states too.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Private businesses outside the statute; criminal trigger requires willful entry plus refusal to depart; one arrest dismissed.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State ban stacks on national facility-order exposure; airports covered by state statute, screening by national.

care_services.exposure: State bans minors' care, restricts adult provision (physicians-only disrupted ~80% of clinic patients), insurance bar, conscience refusals; national orders and proposed rules target care and youth services.
care_services.protection: Court injunctions partially block care bans (status on appeal unresolved); legal-aid FAQ on documents.
care_services.interaction: A visitor needing medication continuation meets physician-only and conscience-refusal rules.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National orders frame gender diversity as deception/mutilation; counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' groups; justice department cash-reward memorandum; state leaders frame trans women as deceptive threats.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostile framing licenses police and enforcement across all other stages; mixed with a 2020 employment-discrimination ruling and hate-crime statute.

minors_guardians.exposure: State ban on all minors' care; national order criminalises teachers facilitating social transition; national subpoena of minors' hospital records; national custody-modification laws on gender-affirming care; state sports exclusion and menstrual-data proposal.
minors_guardians.protection: Court injunctions partially block care bans; city sanctuary designation for one town.
minors_guardians.interaction: Travelling with a trans minor risks care interruption and, if care is sought, investigation exposure.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 3.7 trans women murdered per 100k/yr, near top of national law-hostility scale and a 'Do Not Travel' flag; police arrested a trans student at the capitol.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime law excludes gender identity; commission enforces sex-discrimination reading in employment/housing/accommodations; ~55% of population under local inclusive ordinances.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: The rate exceeds background and coexists with state-hostile law; remedy machinery is partial and coverage-gapped.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Trespass statute untested on merits; licence/birth-certificate rules' litigation status unknown; airport application of facility law undocumented; advisory current status unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Multiple orders enjoined; ACLU litigation pending; running legal-aid FAQ; case dismissed on standing (no substantive ruling either way).
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unresolved litigation means operative exposure depends on timing of travel; unknowns extrapolate downward given documented hostile enforcement elsewhere.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar tier-1 universal facility rule with criminal trigger and no remedy, plus one arrest. This jurisdiction is harsher: the rule spans schools, parks, airports, adds document-fraud treatment and a hostile national layer with visa-refusal exposure, so it sits below 0.35-A.

0.45-A has a polite public, no organised targeting and one prosecuted assault. Here the state is 'Do Not Travel' flagged with a 3.7/100k trans-women murder rate and a documented capitol arrest; national custody abuses add severity, placing this below 0.45-A.

0.25-D combines a universal facilities/ward rule with police stops and extortion threats. This case has comparable universal facility exposure plus entry-document exposure, but fewer documented recurrent police stops; slightly above 0.25-D.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller faces a two-layer hostile regime. The national layer exposes every entrant: visa officers instructed to refuse and consider lifetime fraud findings where sex is doubted, a passport policy prompting allied travel advisories, and documented trans-specific abuse in national custody. The state layer adds a criminal-trespass facilities ban reaching airports, schools and parks, marker-mismatch treated as fraud, restricted adult care, and no gender-identity hate-crime protection — with a documented arrest. Enforcement is sporadic (one dismissed prosecution), but universal-exposure rules are rated by the possibility every traveller carries, and the hostility is state-authored. Partial injunctions and local ordinances do not reach the operative exposures. Combined: high risk, near the 0.30 mark.
